playstyle: TREASURE IS THE ENGINE; DRAGONS AND COMBAT ARE PAYOFFS THE ENGINE BUYS. The engine itself is non-creature — enchantments, artifacts and lands — because this pod wipes creatures constantly and an engine built on bodies resets to zero. Treasure buys cards, buys damage, and buys Dragons at the discount Eminence grants free from the command zone. CREATURES ARE A REAL SECOND MODE, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT: 26 creatures, 15 of them fliers, 15 Dragons, and the deck attacks when the coast is clear. The rule is VALUE ON ENTRY OR ON DEATH, NEVER ON PERSISTENCE — a wipe cannot undo a trigger that already resolved. Scourge of Valkas and Terror of the Peaks ping on every Dragon entering, Lathliss makes a 5/5 token per nontoken Dragon which triggers both again, Gadrak and Pitiless Plunderer pay when creatures die. Big fliers are wanted; they are simply not what the deck depends on. NOT DRAGON TYPAL: the cost-reducer and tutor package is cut, because Eminence already discounts Dragons for free and those cards were paying twice for one effect.
commander_rationale: The Ur-Dragon is kept for three reasons that compound, none of which is casting him. (1) EMINENCE from the command zone discounts 15 Dragons by {1} each, from turn zero. (2) FIVE-COLOUR ACCESS, and it is only worth something if SPENT — Treasures tap for any colour, so the deck takes the best treasure card in every colour instead of sitting inside three. Measured, that means BLACK: Black Market Connections, Revel in Riches, Pitiless Plunderer, Crux of Fate, Toxic Deluge, Demonic Tutor. BLUE IS DELIBERATELY UNSPENT — its best cards for this deck are colourless ones needing no splash at all. (3) THE IDENTITY UPGRADES THE DECK'S OWN FIXERS: Arcane Signet and Commander's Sphere tap for any colour in the commander's identity, which is WUBRG here and would be RGW under a Naya commander. Casting him is upside, never the plan: at {4}{W}{U}{B}{R}{G} an RGW base supplies W, R and G and two Treasures cover U and B. His attack trigger is unused upside, not a line.
mana: MANA BASE IS RGW ONLY — no Swamps, no black duals, 36 lands. Black is cast entirely off Treasures plus four fixers (Chromatic Lantern turns all 36 lands into black sources; Commander's Sphere, Arcane Signet and Mox Jasper each tap for any colour). That is roughly 31 ways to make black with zero black lands. Treasure-making LANDS ride free in the mana base at no spell cost: Treasure Vault, Fountainport, Mines of Moria, Volatile Fault, The Gold Saucer.
design_rules: A card that does two jobs beats a card that does one. Target: 14+ cards doing three or more of {treasure, body, draw, non-combat damage, ramp, removal, protection, token multiplier, survives-a-wipe}.
Off-colour cards must be SORCERY-SPEED ONE-SHOTS. An instant held up means Treasures kept untapped across every opponent's turn — the exact structural failure the 2026-08-25 debrief found in Edgar.
Value on entry or on death, never on persistence.
The engine's core must survive a creature wipe: prefer enchantments, artifacts and lands for treasure generation.
No card is included for tribal synergy alone. Dragons earn slots as payoffs.
win_conditions: ONE alternate win keyed to the engine: Revel in Riches at ten Treasures, which also MAKES them off opponents' creatures dying. Jaya's Immolating Inferno is a SINK, not a win — it converts Treasure into lethal at each opponent. Hellkite Tyrant is a combat-gated STEAL (the twenty-artifact clause is a rider on its combat trigger); the pod runs 7-12 artifacts each, so a connect is worth taking, but it is a threat among 15 Dragons rather than a line the deck builds toward.
